resources.string: Lets taps and swipes on your car\'s screen control this phone while Car Mirror is mirroring. It only performs those taps: it can\'t read what\'s on your screen or what you type, and nothing is collected or sent anywhere.

Car Mirror blanks your car's screen while the car is moving, and brings the picture back a few seconds after you stop. Maps are paused too.

To know when you're moving, it reads your phone's GPS speed while mirroring. Location stays on your phone: it is never stored or sent anywhere.

Next, Android will ask for location. Choose Precise and While using the app. You can switch this off any time under Settings.
To notice when your phone connects to your car, Android needs the Nearby devices permission. You can allow it later in Settings → Apps → Car Mirror → Permissions.
Why Car Mirror uses a VPN

Your Tesla's browser won't open the kind of address a phone hotspot uses. Car Mirror gives your phone one extra address that the car will open, and Android only allows that through its VPN feature.

This VPN carries no traffic. Your apps use the internet exactly as before, nothing is sent through it, and nothing leaves your phone except the picture going to your car over the hotspot.

Next, Android will ask you to allow the connection.
Mirroring needs the VPN step so your car can reach your phone.
Screen sharing was cancelled. Tap Start mirroring to try again.

To turn your phone\'s brightness down while mirroring, Android needs you to let Car Mirror modify system settings. It only changes brightness, and puts yours back when you stop mirroring.\n\nOn the next screen, switch on Allow.

Touch control lets taps and swipes on your car's screen control this phone while Car Mirror is mirroring.

To do that, Car Mirror needs Android's Accessibility permission. It uses it only to perform those taps. It can't read what's on your screen or what you type, and nothing is collected or sent anywhere.

In Settings, open Car Mirror touch control (it may be under Installed apps or Downloaded apps) and turn it on. You can turn it off there any time.

\n\nIf it\'s greyed out or Android says \"App was denied access\": tap App info below, then ⋮ (top right) → Allow restricted settings, then come back and switch it on. Android asks this once, for apps not installed from the Play Store.
